title: What's new in AL and Tools
summary: The session follows one sample app, a late fee extension, through build, evolve, test, review and support steps, with Peter and Stefan presenting. It starts with the AL MCP and a new AL language server, used in Copilot to search the environment, get free object IDs and trace code. It then covers language and platform changes: interface default implementations with a required-pending attribute, public package resources, integer to big integer fields, keys mixing base and extension fields, and translation IDs with namespaces. Small clarity changes follow, then data-driven tests, test handlers, a static call graph analysis in the AL tool, and two new MCP proxy commands for agent-started profiles and snapshots. The speakers close by advising teams to adopt the steps one at a time.

chapters.title: Intro: late fee app and the two building blocks (AL MCP, AL language server)
Discover: what is already there in the environment
Demo: symbol search, next object ID and language server in Copilot
Evolve: interface default implementations and required pending
Overview of sharing resources, big integer, merged table extensions, translation namespaces
Public resource folders and consuming them by app ID
Big integer sequences and extension indexes
Small clarity changes: tooltips, audit names, IsDirty
Test handlers and default test handlers
Static call graph analysis for review
Support: profiles and snapshots started by agents (MCP proxies)

features.name: AL MCP server with environment search
features.description: The AL MCP, launched in the previous release, gives AI agents tools to work with AL projects. It can now search the connected environment, tell which app owns each object (with app version), and work with workspace and projects.
features.status_evidence_quote: We have the ALMCP that we launched uh in the last release
prerequisites: Copilot configured with the AL MCP

features.name: AL symbol search with source = environment
features.description: The symbol search tool has a new parameter called source, where you can choose environment. This lets it look up symbols on the remote server, so you do not need to download symbols or set up dependencies first. Demoed by finding Customer Ledger Entry in the base app of the sandbox.
prerequisites: Connected sandbox environment

features.name: Get next object ID tool (MCP)
features.description: A new MCP tool reads the app.json of the current project, works out the defined ID ranges and suggests free object IDs. In the demo it suggested 50,100 and 50,102 style IDs because 50,1xx was already used.
prerequisites: Project with ID ranges in app.json

features.name: AL language server (LSP)
features.description: A new standalone AL language server gives project-aware language intelligence over the language server protocol, so it is no longer tied to Visual Studio Code. In the demo, Copilot used go to definition and find references through it to explain how the fee calculation is used.
prerequisites: LSP configured in the Copilot setup

features.name: Default implementation for interface methods
features.description: Interface methods can now have a default implementation, so consumers do not have to implement newly added methods. This allows interfaces to grow over many releases without breaking existing implementers. A consumer sees a warning that a default exists, and can still implement its own logic.

features.name: Required pending attribute
features.description: Together with default implementations, an attribute lets the interface author tell consumers that implementing the new method will become mandatory later, for example in the next major or two majors. Consumers get a warning with a mandatory message instead of a break.
caveats: Breaking at some point, based on the publisher's own policy
prerequisites: Default implementation on the interface method

features.name: Public package resources
features.description: Resources stored in an app can now be shared across app boundaries by marking resource folders as public. Other apps can list apps with public resources by filter, list resources per app ID, and get them as JSON or text by passing the provider app ID, without a dependency. Getting a resource by app ID only works for public resources; your own private resources still work with the normal functions without an app ID.
caveats: Getting a private resource with an app ID gives an error
Getting a resource that does not exist gives an error
Be careful with hard dependencies on a specific app's public resources, since they may stop shipping it
prerequisites: Publisher marks the resource folders as public

features.name: Integer to big integer field change
features.description: A field type can be changed from integer to big integer while keeping existing rows, aimed at ledger or sequence entries that run out of numbers. The compiler, AppSourceCop and the comparison with the previous app version show warnings, for example implicit conversion from big integer to integer and possible runtime overflow, but the change is allowed without copying data or keeping a parallel implementation.
caveats: Changing the type does not update the places where the value is used, for example assigning it to an integer field
Implicit conversion may overflow at runtime
Dependent apps that have not changed to big integer can overflow at runtime
Comparison against the previous app version reports further errors
prerequisites: AppSourceCop and comparison against the previous app version to see the warnings

features.name: Keys spanning base and extension fields
features.description: Table extensions are now merged into the base table, so a key can span both base table and table extension fields at the same time. Described as a long requested addition. With the changes in how the SQL side of extensions is managed, this gives an index that is useful for reading data by the new policy group field.

features.name: Namespaces in translation IDs
features.description: Translation XLIFF files can now be generated with fully qualified names (including the namespace) as the ids instead of hash keys built from the name. This avoids collisions between objects with the same name in different namespaces and makes the ids readable. It is first mentioned in the overview and then demoed.
caveats: Old hash-key ids could collide when names exist more than once in the global space
prerequisites: Namespaced objects
Translation file setting in app.json for translations with namespaces

features.name: Action inherits page tooltip
features.description: An action that uses RunObject no longer needs its own tooltip, because the tooltip comes from the target page. The description is kept in one place and reused across many pages.
prerequisites: Action defined with RunObject

features.name: Audit name system fields (created by / modified by full name)
features.description: New system fields on the record hold the created by and modified by full names next to the user ids. They can be placed on pages in code and are now customizable through personalization or customization, which was hard before because they were only rendered in the client.

features.name: IsDirty on Record and RecordRef
features.description: A new IsDirty method on Record and RecordRef tests whether a record has changed. It lets you ask the user whether to save, instead of comparing fields by hand.

features.name: Explicit read isolation for isolated storage
features.description: Read isolation is now an explicit option when reading from isolated storage. You can state read committed with an update lock instead of leaving it implied. It is only mentioned briefly in the summary.

features.name: Data-driven tests (test data source)
features.description: One test method can run many scenarios taken from a data test source that lists test cases, such as overdue, not overdue and rounding. The data for each case is built on demand, and the platform runs the test once for every entry in the data set.
caveats: Only the new syntax is shown here; a dedicated session in the launch event covers data-driven testing in depth
prerequisites: A data test source implementing the list of test cases

features.name: Test run from command line with structured JSON output
features.description: The whole test suite can be run from the command line. It returns structured JSON with pass, fail and skip counts and a real exit code, so a failed assertion fails the build.

features.name: Test handlers (test lifecycle hooks)
features.description: Test handlers keep setup and reporting out of the test logic. A handler is specified on the test codeunit and offers hooks before and after the test codeunit run, the test procedure run and each test case run. The demo uses a logger handler that traces while tests run.
prerequisites: Handler implementing the test handler interface/enum implementation

features.name: Default test handlers
features.description: A default test handler can be added by extending the default test handlers enum with an implementation, so it covers all test cases that run. It can implement just one hook, such as before test codeunit run, and be used next to handlers on a specific test codeunit.
caveats: A warning appears when only some methods are implemented because there is a default implementation that must be overridden for custom behavior
prerequisites: Enum extension of the default test handlers enum with an implementation of the test handler

features.name: Static call graph analysis (graph command in the AL tool)
features.description: The AL .NET tool gets a graph command that builds a call graph across an extension and its dependencies. You or your coding agent can query it, for example to find who can call an internal procedure, where the public boundary is, which public entry points to review, and the path from a page action to the method. It is a static offline analysis, so the extracted output can be compared between versions.
caveats: Extraction compiles all specified apps and takes time, so it was done in advance for the demo
Static analysis works on the extracted data, not on the project as it is now like the LSP
A separate full session on the graph tool will cover querying and visualizing the graph in more detail; a link is in the description
prerequisites: al .NET tool, where the agentic tools live
Run the extraction first over the apps you specify (compiles them)

features.name: Launch profiling MCP proxy
features.description: A new AL tool command that lets a coding agent start, monitor and stop a performance profile and look at the results, using the same kind of tooling and parameters as in Visual Studio Code. The agent needs to know the environment and the profile speed settings.
caveats: No actual profiling was run in the demo, only the command and its parameters were shown
The developer still has to judge what the captured evidence means
Work happens on the server, the proxy is only an interface for the client
prerequisites: The AL tool
An agentic framework that can use the MCP proxy
A target environment

features.name: Launch snapshot MCP proxy
features.description: A new AL tool command that lets agents target a specific environment and tenant and start a snapshot recording while a user is working. This captures values and the call stack to find a bottleneck, an error or another issue. It has fewer parameters than the profiling proxy.
caveats: No snapshot is run on the client, all work happens on the server
The developer still has to judge what the evidence means
prerequisites: The AL tool
A target environment and tenant

quotes.text: You don't have to download the symbols. You don't have to create the dependent species before you can actually find the symbols.
quotes.why_it_matters: States the main benefit of searching symbols on the connected environment instead of local symbol files.

quotes.text: This is critical for allowing you to extend the interfaces over time.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains the design reason for default implementations on interfaces.

quotes.text: So now with the default implementation we can extend an interface and build our solution across many releases without breaking any of our consumers.
quotes.why_it_matters: Summarizes the outcome: interfaces can evolve without breaking implementers.

quotes.text: they're actually merged into uh the the base uh table and that means that a key can now span uh both base and extension fields at the same time
quotes.why_it_matters: A design change in table extensions that enables keys across base and extension fields.

quotes.text: The public resources are actually consumable without a dependency.
quotes.why_it_matters: Consumers of public resources do not need a dependency on the providing app.

quotes.text: if you try to get a private resource by and providing the app ID, you will get an error.
quotes.why_it_matters: A limitation: only resources in public folders can be fetched with a provider app ID.

quotes.text: So be mindful about taking hard dependencies on specific apps on public resources because if they stop shipping it,
quotes.why_it_matters: Warns that runtime errors occur if a provider app stops shipping a resource.

quotes.text: that sometimes the ledger entries or some of the other the sequence entries run out of numbers.
quotes.why_it_matters: Gives the real-world reason for the integer to big integer change.

quotes.text: So we made it possible for you to switch to big integer by changing the type.
quotes.why_it_matters: States the design decision to allow changing a field to big integer for large customers whose entries run out of numbers.

quotes.text: Just changing the type itself does not change all the places where you use this value.
quotes.why_it_matters: Warns that a big integer change needs follow-up edits in code that uses the field.

quotes.text: but it's still allowed and it will still pass through and you can actually do this change without having to copy data
quotes.why_it_matters: Shows the type change passes the breaking-change check and needs no data copy or parallel implementation.

quotes.text: This will now generate XL files with a fully qualified name as the ids.
quotes.why_it_matters: Describes the namespace-aware translation ids that avoid collisions between same-named objects.

quotes.text: These are not fields that I have created. They're part of the system fields on the record now.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains that created by and modified by full names are new built-in system fields, not custom ones.

quotes.text: run the whole suite from the command line and get structured JSON with pass fail and skip counts plus a real exit code
quotes.why_it_matters: Gives the concrete CI outcome: structured results and an exit code that fails the build.

quotes.text: So for every single entry that exists in this data set, this platform will execute this test and provide the result for it.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains how data-driven tests run: one test method executes once per data set entry.

quotes.text: So I have the flexibility of handling things outside the test case in a common way both globally but also specifically for a specific test code unit.
quotes.why_it_matters: Summarizes that test handlers work at both global and per-codeunit level.

quotes.text: Counter to the LSP which is actually looking at the project as it is now.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains how the graph analysis differs from the language service protocol tool.

quotes.text: This is a static thing that we can do offline as long as we extract uh the information that we need to query on beforehand.
quotes.why_it_matters: States the call graph is an offline static analysis that needs an up-front extraction step.

quotes.text: coding agents can now capture the performance profiles and the snapshot recordings themselves through dedicated MCP uh tools with no active debugging session
quotes.why_it_matters: Core announcement: agents can start profiles and snapshots without a debugging session set up by the developer.

quotes.text: You still need to judge uh what the evidence that it find means
quotes.why_it_matters: Sets the limit: the agent captures evidence but the human interprets it.

quotes.text: Why are these called proxies? This is because the actual work all happens on the server.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains the design decision behind the proxy naming.

quotes.text: There's no snapshot or um performance profiling being done on the client side. It's all being done on the server side.
quotes.why_it_matters: Clarifies where capture runs, relevant for environment access and expectations.

quotes.text: this release has been around making agents more capable making it easier for agents to work with the code
quotes.why_it_matters: Summarizes the theme of the whole release for AL and tools.

quotes.text: You don't need to adopt everything at once. Start with a gap that you have today
quotes.why_it_matters: Practical adoption advice from the presenters.
